maybe I should stop calling it that, lol

anyway, after some small fixes and finetunings, we decided to add a chat to the website as well

currently it requires a hive account to use and a minimum threshold on your reputation to prevent unwanted spam/unwanted content



![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/acidyo/23tGTUZXxqaXMzxEKbqnquvGBGk56gnSnJrErMU9KK4b6Re66uCjAh3SUDPSSKLycesWK.png)


the cool thing with it is that when you drop a song link (youtube/spotify/itunes) it shows a nice preview and also loads a youtube embed link so that other chatters can instantly check what someone shared and play it there on the website through the youtube embed. 

Idea here is that if you're listening to a song you wanna share with people who may be active on the site, you probably haven't scrobbled it yet, so others may not be able to find it in the scrobble history, thus by linking it in chat and allowing others to easily load it up, they can scrobble it for the first time through the chat before it even is scrobbled from outside sources through the extenion

If that makes sense, maybe? :D

Anyway, other than some styling here and there I've mostly been working on a few minigames for scrobble.life! 

Now it's still in the works and some of them require curation, but to spoil some of them: 

#### Hang the DJ

> "Hang the DJ" is a Black Mirror episode (Season 4, Episode 4) whose title and thematic origin lie in the 1986 song "Panic" by The Smiths.


This is going to be a simple hangman style game where you have to guess all the correct letters to fill in song name and artist name. 


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/acidyo/Enyn31kF1B2fRRuRdgTEsRq1kgCSErnLwnoetqGD4D8UtJHxyy7m551Xx1eeWGdeyQg.png)

#### Scroddle

Naming isn't that imaginative on this one, as you may have guessed it, it's a similar mechanic to wordle or hive wordle but targeted towards music with movies having its own version! The caveats here are that it's not only 5 letter words but it can range from 4 to 6. 


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/acidyo/23swbZk1gUneGxmf25jTUJGQTm3S6E53bWwhq2w3fWX7Jh2DEGUjHiNY1mYTUeapqPD5A.png)

#### Scroddle Mix

Name also temporary for this one. 

The idea in this is that it's a lot more complicated than Scroddle, but mixed with an assist in the form of hangman. Some times the answer it's looking for is a song name, some times it's a band name, the assist is always the other. 

A simple explanation: 

Let's assume we're looking for the songname Crawling by Linkin Park. 

You start similar like wordle but you can see it's looking for a 8 letter name, so let's say you guess "Umbrella" on your first attempt. 

It'll show that you got the R correct but with a yellow color, meaning it's not in the right spot, however, it will show the R in Linkin Pa**R**k. The same would go for the letter L and A, they're yellow and not in the right spot but the artist name will then show as L_ _ _ _ _ _ a r _.

Thus while the songs are harder to guess and may be longer in certain difficulties, it gives you hints along the way in the artist name.

This is still in experimental mode, I'm asking a few friends to test them out as they're way better at wordle than myself, but needless to say this needs to be a curated list with one answer per day in several difficulties. At least that's the plan. 

Some of these games will also be based on your own scrobble history, so not just random popular songs/artists.

Which cues me to the next game I'm working on, this one will due to the above require users to have at leat 500 scrobbles in their history to play, however as it needs something to select from. 

The game here is that it plays up to 3 songs in 3 tiered difficulties, it attempts to start the song somewhere where it's recognizable and play a 15 second snippet where you have 15 seconds to guess song name and artist. Bonus points for both, but just getting one correct is enough to earn some points along with a speed calculation based on how quick you were to guess it. 

After you've guessed, it'll tell you your score and show the youtube embed of the song you guessed or failed to. 

Anyway, these have not been as easy to implement so it's taken some extra time and prompts, but hopefully you can try them out soon, in the meantime, try get to 500 scrobbles so you can be the first to test one of them! 


___ 

Let me know what you think of the games, there'll be options similar to hivewordle to post results to snaps based on how you did without spoiling the daily answers, etc. 

If you have any other cool ideas, let us know and we'll see what we can do!

--- One of the most important elements, capable of steering our emotions and influencing parts of a film’s plot, is the soundtrack, hose songs or musical themes playing in the background. Although we may not realise it, they often shape how we feel when watching a film. And not only that, but there are soundtracks that define a film; when we hear them out of context, they make us remember it and transport us straight back to it. >Una de las características más importantes y que puede dirigir las emociones y partes de la trama de una película es la banda sonora, aquellas canciones o temas musicales que suenan de fondo, aunque no nos demos cuenta pero que muchas veces condicionan lo que sentimos al ver una película. Y no sólo eso, sino que hay bandas sonoras que caracterizan a la película y que al escucharlas fuera del contexto nos hacen recordarla, nos llevan a ella directamente. --- ![Image_1778087185947.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23xVRTBfLiecHQ5kqLjkh8yLfdpWaXgKZbwv3F7gtqTE8P9PTNAr1XFtVST1GwmyAeXp4.jpg) ![Searador video yh.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/EoCj3fkLfDyM1LGXmuEEEUunY7K2H9aJ92pw7L2JoBxDeD4XiDZ8SDgs5zdayTYiWdE.png) ---
SPANISH VERSION (click here!)

La música genera emociones, y en una película es algo fundamental, porque pueden producir tristeza si se trata de un drama, o terror si es una película de ese género. Hay bandas sonoras que dan energía, otras que son propias de películas de acción y hasta han bandas sonoras o temas puntuales de películas de comedia. Por todo ello elegí como tema del mes y por supuesto, es un tema, pueden desarrollarlo aún fuera del mes, es sólo una sugerencia, ideas para desarrollar reseñas sobre videos, en este caso sobre el tema que les traigo hoy. Si miro o si me pongo a pensar en las bandas sonoras de películas que me gusta me doy cuenta que todas tienen algo en común y es que son orquestales, con energía, con fuerza, aunque también las hay las canciones suaves y melancólicas, eso dependerá del estilo de película y del compositor. Es verdad que cuesta conseguir canales oficiales de este tema, pero por ejemplo en mi caso lo que hice fue buscar el canal del compositor, por citarles uno, Hans Zimmer, que quizás muchos no lo conozcan por el nombre, pero cuando sepan la música que ha compuesto y para que películas se darán cuenta.

Music evokes emotions, and in a film this is essential, because it can evoke sadness in a drama, or fear in a horror film. Some soundtracks are energising, others are typical of action films, and there are even soundtracks or specific tracks from comedy films. That’s why I’ve chosen this as the theme of the month, and of course, it’s just a theme; you can explore it even after the month is over, it’s simply a suggestion, ideas for writing reviews of videos, in this case on the topic I’m bringing you today. If I look back or start thinking about the film soundtracks I like, I realise they all have something in common: they’re orchestral, energetic and powerful, though there are also soft, melancholic tracks, that depends on the style of the film and the composer. It’s true that it’s hard to find official channels on this topic, but in my case, for example, what I did was look for the composer’s channel, to name just one, Hans Zimmer. Perhaps many of you won’t recognise the name, but once you hear the music he’s composed and realise which films they’re for, you’ll know who he is. --- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JZeNYaTmVP4&list=OLAK5uy_kJntk1t2jZLBJiqhTgEXmghjA8AIJEiAg
*[Source](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JZeNYaTmVP4&list=OLAK5uy_kJntk1t2jZLBJiqhTgEXmghjA8AIJEiAg)*
![Searador video yh.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/EoCj3fkLfDyM1LGXmuEEEUunY7K2H9aJ92pw7L2JoBxDeD4XiDZ8SDgs5zdayTYiWdE.png) ---
SPANISH VERSION (click here!)

Me gusta todo tipo de películas, pero sobre todo las de misterio, ciencia ficción, acción y fantasía. Por supuesto muchas otras. Pero los ejemplos que les traigo son precisamente eso, ejemplos de bandas sonoras y que me encantan, además de que le dan un estilo particular a la película. La banda sonora de Piratas del Caribe, es una de mis favoritas, tiene una energía poderosa, es orquestal como les comentaba y pertenece al compositor que les cité arriba. Él ha hecho la banda sonora para muchas películas. Pueden buscar en su canal oficial y se van a sorprender. Cara canción de la lista de reproducción que ha desarrollado para esta saga de películas es fabulosa, tiene una canción para cada momento y al escucharlas me recuerda esas partes de la película en donde aparecían, me hace revivir las escenas como si la estuviera viendo. Ese creo es uno de los objetivos de las bandas sonoras, además de generar emociones varias.

I like all kinds of films, but especially thrillers, science fiction, action and fantasy. There are, of course, many others. But the examples I’m giving you are just that: examples of soundtracks that I love, as well as ones that give the film a distinctive style. The Pirates of the Caribbean soundtrack is one of my favourites; it has a powerful energy, is orchestral as I mentioned, and is by the composer I mentioned above. He has composed soundtracks for many films. You can check out his official channel and you’ll be surprised. Every single track on the playlist he’s created for this film series is fabulous; there’s a song for every moment, and listening to them reminds me of those parts of the film where they appeared, making me relive the scenes as if I were watching them. I think that’s one of the aims of soundtracks, as well as evoking a range of emotions. --- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TFk8L6S3Ru4&list=OLAK5uy_khNWSY28-tKQdFS5m73n532AaMvPV2mLs

Hay tantos ejemplos, que me quedaría corta al mencionar muchos de ellos. Por ejemplo, me gusta la banda sonora de películas como: El Padrino, Matrix, Gladiador, Drácula, Batman, Van Helsing y muchas más. Para darles un dato más este compositor que tanto me gusta, Hans Zimmer, ha realizado también muchas de las bandas sonoras de video juegos. Pueden consultar su página oficial. El segundo ejemplo que les traigo es la banda sonora de la película Van Helsing, cuyo compositor es Alan Silvestri, también es una banda sonora orquestal y me encanta. Es fundamental para guiar la película en todos los momentos de acción, suspenso, fantasía, de lucha, batalla entre el vampiro y su cazador.

There are so many examples that I wouldn’t do them justice by mentioning them all. For instance, I love the soundtracks to films such as: The Godfather, The Matrix, Gladiator, Dracula, Batman, Van Helsing and many more. To give you one more piece of information, Hans Zimmer, a composer I’m particularly fond of, has also composed many video game soundtracks. You can check out his official website. The second example I’d like to share is the soundtrack to the film Van Helsing, composed by Alan Silvestri; it’s also an orchestral soundtrack and I love it. It’s essential in guiding the film through all the moments of action, suspense, fantasy, and the struggle and battle between the vampire and his hunter. --- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vsMWVW4xtwI&list=RDvsMWVW4xtwI&start_radio=1
*[Source](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vsMWVW4xtwI&list=RDvsMWVW4xtwI&start_radio=1)*

SPANISH VERSION (click here!)

Y para el tercer ejemplo no les traigo una banda sonora, sino una canción que es también orquestal pero que esa sola canción marca un hito en la historia de una saga de películas muy famosa. Mi hermano es fan de esa saga y más de esa canción y me inspiró para traerla como ejemplo para el tema del mes. Con esto quiero decir que no necesariamente tiene que ser una lista de reproducción, una banda sonora completa de una película, sino que pude ser una canción característica, como la tienen muchas películas. Este es el caso de Stars Wars, quien no conoce esta canción o quien al escucharla no evoca la película.

nd for the third example, I’m not bringing you a soundtrack, but a song that is also orchestral, yet that single track marks a milestone in the history of a very famous film series. My brother is a fan of that series, and even more so of that song, and he inspired me to include it as an example for this month’s theme. By this I mean that it doesn’t necessarily have to be a playlist or a complete film soundtrack; it could simply be a signature song, as many films have. This is the case with Star Wars, who doesn’t know this song, or who, upon hearing it, doesn’t think of the film? --- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k2C5TjS2sh4&list=RDk2C5TjS2sh4&start_radio=1
*[Source](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k2C5TjS2sh4&list=RDk2C5TjS2sh4&start_radio=1)*

Hay muchas otras canciones particulares, como la canción de la película Mujer Bonita, interpretada por Roxette. Hay muchas películas, de diversos géneros y casi todas tienen una canción que las caracteriza, como otro ejemplo que es Top Gun. Y así podría estar citando muchas de ellas. Creo que al nombrar la película en sus mentes surge sin duda la canción sin que la escuchen. Ese el objetivo de estas bandas sonoras o canciones en particular. Lo importante de todo esto es que hagan una reseña con una o varias bandas sonoras, pero sobre todo lo importante es la experiencia de ustedes, que comenten o nos cuenten porque les gusta esa banda sonora, que sentimientos o emociones les producen, porque les gusta esa película si es que el gusto por película y banda sonora están relacionadas, o si hay alguna anécdota especial con los ejemplos que han elegido. Dejen volar su creatividad. Recuerden sus opiniones personales y vivencias son las que cuentan. Esperando les encante el tema del mes, les envío a todos un gran saludo. Hasta pronto. Amonet.

There are many other memorable songs, such as the theme from the film Pretty Woman, performed by Roxette. There are many films across various genres, and almost all of them have a song that defines them, such as Top Gun, to give another example. I could go on listing many more. I think that when you mention the film, the song undoubtedly springs to mind without you even hearing it. That is the purpose of these soundtracks or specific songs. The important thing here is that you write a review featuring one or more soundtracks, but above all, what matters is your own experience: tell us why you like that soundtrack, what feelings or emotions it evokes in you, why you like that film (if your taste in films and soundtracks are related), or if there’s a special anecdote linked to the examples you’ve chosen. Let your creativity run wild. Remember, it’s your personal opinions and experiences that count. Hoping you’ll love this month’s theme, I send you all my best wishes. See you soon. Amonet. --- ![Miniatura 1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23wgYSX78fchqP72SjzNEfu8AnUrpiz6AzYJJKN5f9vpnW4BdDjwSg3ScRC11EkEzkkau.jpg) ---

<center>![PXL_20260502_014142661.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23tkb4P7wwtnoR2q82yr3iu2NLvHtdQL6Ageu4VDDUxbs9BUE23ypFN4TgojbMFCVEPJX.jpg)</center>

-----------------------------

When I left off my post on Wednesday, we were just getting ready to head into the heart of the Zoo lights experience at the John Ball Zoo.  If you missed it, you can [get caught up here](https://peakd.com/hive-193212/@bozz/john-ball-zoo-lantern-festival).  As I said, the photos I shared with you yesterday were sort of the appetizer for what we yet had in store as we made our way up the side of the hills of the zoo.  

I'll tell you right now, unlike a lot of my other posts, this one is going to be mostly photos and very little text.  If that is your jam then cool, I hope you like it.  If you prefer more text, I'll try to do better next week!


<center>![PXL_20260502_013109120.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23tknMR8h551YLtVf2kWkAvuHWv82NxwJDDrYJNbS7bHKhdcetemX3qt461usHj3o8xWp.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_013100900.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23u5bfV4fX3JBxBnVdWyF35amvJAjt5xwKQs2gE9L31EwABfPenKcRMQAkeobHe6bxs5j.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_013210574.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23tGVupuuGR1yLgSPH2a52czfc5fc2smQUPSGL85UU1oZ76ir3wpVXtAwmbErMTMNYJMY.jpg)</center>

------------------------------------

The exhibit itself is broken up into a couple of different segments.  Right before what you see above, there was a section that had the different animals of the Chinese Zodiac.  I made sure to take a shot of the Dragon since that is my animal.  Unfortunately, due to the crowd, I wasn't able to get the horse for @mrsbozz.

I'd say the first section was flowers, but I don't think that would be entirely accurate.  I'm not actually sure what the theme was here, perhaps forest.  You be the judge with the following photos.


<center>![PXL_20260502_013246725.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23tS2tcscdKuGHPSohNgMytvMaqF1kRh8hSQpYw7HgmTTyLfgCiytH7oaLXddA2wf5gYw.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_013401182.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23u5XXuVyjfi5uAUM73Tc2bK4gmXSKMnxx5iDUcui46N2NCtEXWesKBAYJyXP21xPV2Br.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_013422688.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23w2cXTd5qz4fdLoctoTgBsyFnNg6UGC1hRWB28ycb6SbLgzXT5x5GV5QomhMBJMKU15y.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_013435175.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23tS2tn4MRqKLUukfRkgmCz6XHn4dwG1VnWGuPgiQcqUJZtXRzaYXiaizJQZrGk8zfRpK.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_013441299.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23tGVutxKJ2bjMSiUBHAteXmHH3LFNYbXARmvJegUhRR2FcoJLWYsaVhyYQs9ivtrJ79q.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_013502150.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23uFKA9e5vNxK8dqQF126w817x8SkDZ44oPTrjzSYRRBBBvoDQ7E4XyZKR3xA9fuq2xxB.jpg)</center>

---------------------------

The trails in this part of the zoo are actually set up as a series of switchbacks, so it gives you an interesting perspective on what is ahead, what is behind, and what is right in front of you.  I loved the giant bees that you see above.  That was probably my favorite part of this section.  Especially the fact that they couldn't sting you!


<center>![PXL_20260502_013533403.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23u5Z9ndWGG8EqZPnjDEG6WAZbKCF7xvSz1NBpHJJiNvFdpSoRWpx88ZQuGAwhezCSX3F.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_013533835.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/EoAaArgxj3HXg7uqMMjvh8r5djUSFvAv2socoU6oUm9A8pniMyDEQajK3BQps3mGc9Z.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_013545036.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23u5vVncSSs94J5PXic1V4LrXBjkhHkrGD31Cvk3skoE1VVm9H9indTGSWdFFmgTohz1D.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_013645472.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23uFK5nqExzsHbHMim6KhBJJH4H8oTqDj83KWswxJ5aWdZt853Uona2ufXEMMxqbnHtgZ.jpg)</center>

------------------------

As we exited the forest section, things started to become even more green if you can believe that and we eventually found ourselves in what I might call a fantasy jungle...


<center>![PXL_20260502_013829448.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23u5vwmcNW8yu69tzdayQGzzBRMbre5TjTBP798WxRPF355GsA9dYSpVKP8gZNR247gR7.jpg)


<center>![PXL_20260502_013858561.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/EoK3xMooRjKjBtgd8J1Ck1qSpWDpoPRXnKkqrAWQKkkpn2W24ao3qCspfjHJ9f27svT.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_013905334.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23vrk1oiUuLycj8o5HMnr3ZR5wcxhmnpbst7ZRWopWYGLm6ryegMCHXARGNHY8bCfBPQL.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_013921737.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23uEqcEG5CVxPV7fCPqRuVqoHC3N7RawpyatmhypNcCyTorQmhf9HwRu6QbVL4PcfLMAa.jpg)</center>


![PXL_20260502_013932858.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23tGTrJUaZPUdEPUyR3tavGvdUgUd2rnBTgWAKs5HRMgr7YGqD3HfEdhmwCUEdvh9uerx.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_013954326.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23wLx4zZsw7xTzzmPndsYzo2Ao5Dhy4SxHNcyrxWu3WGCBKRJ1RhL5r1Hgk4rouHvb64w.jpg)</center>

-------------------------

The greens in this area were pretty intense and it was probably my favorite area of the whole exhibit.  My only complaint is that people clearly can't read the signs.  The first photo is an animatronic display that had sound and movement.  There was a pretty clear sign that said if you were standing to stay to the right and if you were moving along to keep to the left, but people were standing like idiots taking photos on the left.


<center>![PXL_20260502_014234723.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23tbP7Qy6NnPaJZVSbzEWXXYwubogxWBJL12NE96K7EZYcJa9zn89N9cFkMi1M2XtP7pM.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_014237934.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23uQLqra2eQQpUAXXbxR4AykgEDCZcHbu86PgHMQpdufXpJT7aAphDWXiZxWffn3cAzrn.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_014252668.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23tRxWiDXLhAvCYpqzf6dMZNxbLxbak2Peh8H7BtXq2gip5ksnMRb7nirwq1LU7x1jEZo.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_014337270.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23tvAaGgXYxv4vF8cBFVDwwJMY2Z9zkk3b3SPhufnywvB5v5cfYmL8CoztjSARXaGTmYH.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_014313384.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23tkfhLuBtweqBcgByyMzGZuWbsE3iy5Y2oKWd5hGSQGgeQz7ow5iLeVw3KsGeqWEreT2.jpg)</center>

-----------------------

After another small forest area, things started to take on a more aquatic theme. It was in this second forest area that we ran into the owls.  I thought at first it was just noises that they were playing via speakers when I heard the distinct "who who who".  It wasn't until I started looking closer that I realized we were right next to the owl enclosure.  I could see their silhouette in the dark.


<center>![PXL_20260502_014421487.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23tkjm7YwAmdTs6cLiX5X2QwQFnibE4RKEffqD7E9yBwVqZyRVNVFY8E1E9XxzNmSmFfW.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_014459573.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/EoeCvj7zQ1ZBbfxAb1z7mYmoFYs4YZuVwrp8YQ4CPMPk3xBwRYKuatxHgECkKBw48KJ.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_014500474.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23wMMrYMWFH2Mhrq7Pz2B2WCKbcdXzen4riP2TMbgVJ95kFXcjSJtve67Dxzr7DcHK7jh.jpg)</center>

<center>![PXL_20260502_014535625.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/EoCbpBpXpVKTMwPnAXwY6PGVbF1UEoPYayvgVt7ZFESxKUsQPz6dg2gyZWv8JMb5EZe.jpg)</center>

<center>![PXL_20260502_014608462.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23tGvrwEPeZDb4TgQvUkW8Q1NTbkZzjoQA7aUzeUFEebdoBnf1ertq2w1LHwUHv3Ba5wa.jpg)</center>

---------------------------

The last couple of photos above are another example of how the different elevations allowed you to get a different view of the lights.


<center>![PXL_20260502_014623441.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23tRvj1FM7BqopsLMpnfqiU4KvCHazJGVf5k87RP5YUpDiKbpgxJ5MddLtkGymXEWuaTY.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_014631376.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23tkk8EK87g4eui8V77DeSRuAnUuomvqsxy52Xe1CHcY7hkxzon68PHqSkmeagZ7QmfRE.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_014754874.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23tS32QT5VjzwoyF6AhB5fWrR7JL1fPKt2oY4gGNAU88yoF5gAqqxGwXvHbDeXFwVFhBW.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_014811085.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23vsDbhAVjweMi6XT4jyfof65vpHoar25yVmdokUnkSLaZGeyr24XcqwLFkSG7FZL3RmD.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_014854037.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23tkfTsrXCcGJiEgAU6FXZwQrDEvw7br6C6Er77xLGbVmAgcLa8k7maavzVnKLhZveNCg.jpg)</center>


--------------------------

The jellyfish were really cool, but as you can see I also had to get a nice shot of the Slippery When Wet sign as homage to Bon Jovi!


<center>![PXL_20260502_015023490.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/EoCg7qUTr3PTBZA6VDmEwv4d7on2KcGGnCzGMA2cYfSCJXdxTxbMKNLHnKh54GDfgDr.jpg)</center>


<center>[PXL_20260502_015056757.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23uFGsV4L1smFfPGS7VxwEySNuJkWncucJbBfoDEZwGztjcgHmsFpvMSXKKV3KKy8xXBo.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_015215796.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23w2DK6FXyVxCTWLM8MwBV7Nh8qYja7E9vidudhbPvTYArHhiHPEUboE3R1BJPcU7cpi7.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_015222521.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23tbPKxBUm9H83783juNUkgEyMXiMWGom6EcevceePPj2quS9KwtH6m982C2snuD5KGKb.jpg)</center>


<center>![PXL_20260502_015308526.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23tbPY2XmtAeQkiubf5R7V9krRX27Yc5eDVeZZpJsJsbDydFtxidkove9hVsSCAaqhVxo.jpg)</center>

--------------------------

As you can see from some of the photos, it was hard to not get a lot of people in them. It was just that packed.  I have one photo I didn't share where a lady is looking right at me.  She probably thinks I was some kind of creep taking pictures of her, but really I was just trying to get a good vantage of the lights above her.  

At about $30 USD per person, this wasn't the cheapest thing we did all weekend, but it was still a great time and I am glad we went. I don't know if I would do it again now that I have done it once, but it was definitely worth the trip!

Good evening everyone. Today I wanted to do an upside down update. Specifically one lone jalapeno pepper, which came from an upside down plant.


<center>![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmR3uLhzgUBSagpVg5zZkMkn9Rsmmcew3QqF363grR229o/image.png)
</center>

First of all, do you all remember [this](https://hive.blog/hive-140635/@greenthings/why-upside-down-the-jalapenos) post?
<center>
![Jalapen-post.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmenAgvEJ2c36Bk1WEtwaG5A1sS6sUBdarTy8AB2SpNGYh/Jalapen-post.png)
</center>

You can take a look at that old post and compare it to what has happened through out the summer.  Below are the update photos. 

I had put this rectangular pot upside down, double stacked on the counter in my kitchen and I was sprouting jalapeno seeds to plant.

<center>
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNeanjjCuxNbGWCeZwB5iNPh9aiiPPQAmMUSySsweDfAx/image.png)</center>


I waited until all of the holes that I had drilled each had a little baby jalapeno plant growing. Then I flipped the entire planter. I put it outside and the plants began to grow, downward toward the ground.

All of the plants were  sprouted at the same time and many did not make it. I am guessing that  they did not get enough sun, but the one that did move out to the side has tree like stems and it is very strong.  But only one pepper grows.


<center>
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmX8z86mWNyUQJNfZvyMsYFNfA6eNxUHKdZXsKU7XYNpnc/image.png)
</center>

The whole idea of planting things upside down is to have two pots worth of plants growing but only using the space of one pot.

Over the last seven months I have planted everything from cucumbers to tomatoes to spinach on the top side of this pot and nothing sprouted.

<center>
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUtdxCyRmNpKvxytox5i5q3HFZRAje28wE2VnU8XzNnPb/image.png)
</center>


I thought maybe the birds were coming in and stealing the seeds so I put a mesh over the top and zip tied it in place so there's no way they could scoop the seeds out of the dirt.

<center>
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVNgMA91ocv9i4no2SSWVRx5QmgPujKf3hD1x6H6XjACH/image.png)
</center>


Still nothing grew. So the main benefit of using one pot with plants coming out the bottom and out the top was wasted in this case. So, sadly, I only have photos from the bottom.  

#### Only one Jalapeno?
#
**Yes** - that is the sad reality.   

This little plant grew all summer and looks healthy but it never got long enough for me to tie it to the side so it could get some sun.   

The others got plenty of sun and there is evidence that they had flowers blooming but, well maybe, the bees are not used to looking below the pot to find flowers.  

I had tried to pollinate any flowers that I see and I do a lot of that, hundreds per day on my carnivorous plants.

<center>
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbSG6Pqrw4Dh3eWgtegK3ZBcz67RNVw9zCjeMyeMLBPKF/image.png)
</center>

---  

#### Chili peppers...

There is another plant  just above the jalapeno pot.  This one is round.   I planted chili peppers in it and a couple survived and grew, but I did not even get one pepper. 



<center>
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYTi2mCuw6VMxPWApjmTDaQzkdsH5KUV373DfL7oFAtmV/image.png)
</center>

It looks very healthy and you can see evidence of flowers that had budded.  But for some reason, the bees did not get to them, and they never brought forth any chili peppers.


<center>
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPNJRNvbZ3YPxkNeP8z14YCx4VL11nxBSt4XSZhnica5h/image.png)
</center>

Even though this plant was a complete failure on upside down horticulture, I did include it in this post because it is this plant is taking advantage of the main benefit.

<center>Two Plants - One Pot</center>



<center>
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmW1x1qsMXoq3cLfFsTjUiqcaHpYnrALDzf63SRPELtrHn/image.png)
</center>

As you can see, there's a beautiful kale plant growing out the top, which I'm very proud of.

I heard that kale is way better when it's fresh out of the garden rather than store-bought. I am hoping to find out for myself very soon.

I have another *roots-up* plant that I would like to update you on - but that will be a longer post, including Ginger and Turmeric harvesting.  I  will be posting all winter as things still grow here in the cold - 50s and 60s.   Till next time!

Thanks for following and commenting on my posts. Your support is appreciated!

There's a reason why you almost certainly don't know about this band or song.. the same reason why I have never heard this song or heard of this band either   

I've been walking around all day today talking about how much people that I know should have a listen to this song because I heard it the other day and honestly, it is one of the best songs I have ever heard.    

I wish it would pull a "Myspace" and start playing without your permission simply by you being here looking at this..

<center> https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/3/3a/Can-VitaminC-cover-d.jpg
[src](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/3/3a/Can-VitaminC-cover-d.jpg) </center> 

I can't imagine very many people have heard of this band because I am kind of a music-get-around-sort-of-person and I never heard this song or this band until about a week ago and now I think about this song all the time because I believe it is one of those things that is so good that the world may have missed out on something really amazing by never pushing these guys to the forefront.  

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JXsd5W8ofDw&list=RDJXsd5W8ofDw&start_radio=1

This is almost certainly AI but really, I don't care.  This band was formed in 1968 and nobody really knew about them ever and that is a shame.  Maybe their other stuff sucked but this doesn't.   This is awesome.    Tell me this isn't a fantastic song after you listen to it.. for real.   

There is a lot of bands that have come out of the woodwork to try to capitalize on the majesty of this song/band and I think this is probably due to some sort of feature in a recent tv-show or movie that I am unaware of but at the same time I can tell the difference between a song that was made in the 60's and one that was made in a studio in the past 16 weeks.   

Just listen to the song and tell me..... isn't that something special?   I think so .

The band "Can" is the band in question and dear lord, do I wish that I knew who they were when I was in high school or college because I remember a ton of hippie girls who would have immediately been massive fans of me simply for knowing this song.   It's pretty obscure even now and this song has existed since 1970 or so.    How is that possible?

<center> https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/561f21aa7a3a3598b90ab6a9d6b944bcf5a02824/0_40_3000_1799/master/3000.jpg?width=465&dpr=1&s=none&crop=5%3A4
[src](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/561f21aa7a3a3598b90ab6a9d6b944bcf5a02824/0_40_3000_1799/master/3000.jpg?width=465&dpr=1&s=none&crop=5%3A4)</center>

They were never famous, they never made money, they toured a bit apparently, but they never got the recoginition that I feel they deserve.  They are German, so maybe that has something to do with it.  I don't know!  But all i know is that I have only ever heard this one song from them and realize that this is really something special, at least to me.

The reason why this came up was because myself and a friend of mine were talking about how difficult it would have been to find an obscure song just because you heard it a couple of times in the 90's or early 2000's.   We had no Spotify back then, we had YouTube maybe, but not just everything was uploaded to it and something like this would have taken a while to get there.  

The only way that someone would have ever known about "CAN" back in those times, which wasn't even that long ago, would have been to have someone point it out to you, probably on some sort of rare record collection.   Man, things were different back then.)

Listen to the song and get back to me.  I think it is quite special and if this tiny German band can make even a little bit of money off of it I think that is a good thing.

I was thinking this morning about a comment on one of my blog posts that the older the person got, the less they believed in science. That's a fair call when science can be used to justify agendas, or that seemingly verified truths are debunked, that data can be manipulated and results skewed. I like science. It's discovered some pretty awesome stuff. I'm a science fiction fan. I'm married to a guy with a degree in astrophysics just because he was stoned and wanted to know how the world works, so went to uni to do some maths and shit. 

I mean we always have to circle the question whether the science is the *ulimate* authority, or whether it's just the best tool for *testing* reality and truth. They're  not even the same thing, even if we treat them as if they are. 

Things get messy when you start tugging on that thread, because I start getting into that realm of 'oh not everything is verifiable by science' as an excuse to defend absolute bollocks. Jamie'll say that about star signs,  and I *like* astrology and still can't shake it as *just* a pattern we've made up about ourselves to understand ourselves. It feels true for me, really deeply true, and I'm unwilling to discount it as a knowledge system. 


![b384e77d-7665-4142-bdf7-633989d2a67d-1_all_544.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/23vi3jc5DuHozka4BUQDHRdJBePywzdnCnPBDXKTDLg1a1eESv9FLQApDacreyZ2LUwk4.jpg)


So yeah. Things can feel really right and still be wrong according to 'science'. It's a subject Jamie and I often disagree on. 

But going the other way — pretending that only what’s been measured and verified counts as real — doesn’t quite sit properly with me either. We have to know that science is super powerful but it's also pretty human - it follows trends and government priorities and funding. I believe in plant medicine and the knowledge that's come down through grandmothers about herbs, for example, and just because they haven't funded tests into how comfrey can *knit bone*, as it's folk name suggests, doesn't mean it's not *truth*. It just hasn't had that focus on it *yet*. Science is always correcting itself, which is awesome, but that means what we 'know' according to science is always, always shifting. It's fucking *mercurial*. 

Even Jamie will totally agree that there's a layer that doesn't come from studies or data - some things we just *feel* things are true. But then he'd turn around and say firstly, there's a heap of universal truths you can't argue with, and that perhaps we just haven't found the right tools *yet*. 

![b384e77d-7665-4142-bdf7-633989d2a67d-1_all_18192.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/23wgRzVUBCMssrww2B72K42PtV2mpQbMxwCWLxLoCAVJbFkZGjkjdWNa5LjLfVzEvi49E.jpg)

I keep thinking about how I've always had this utter belief, this undeniable faith, that the natural world isn't inert - that animals and plants and even places carry a lot more than their physical parts. Kids will start there even before they are taught, giving rocks names or picking up on 'energy' in trees and forests even if we're looking at it as something separate to us. 

So on the way into work, I was thinking about how there's this innate, pre science instinct to attribute awareness to the world, like a default setting, and that what we call the scientific worldview is just the learned behaviour over the top of it all. Because how often does science 'prove' or circle back to stuff we 'knew' all along? Not in a hippie 'the forest has a spirit' kinda way, but how they've only recently 'proved' that trees communicate through fungal networks, that plants respond to stress, that systems in nature are way more interconneccted and responsive than science used to believe. They don't call it 'animism' - it's just different language to describe what we always *knew*, whether on some deep tribal, cultural level, or just a suspicion or a feeling. 

It's like the problem of consciousness - we dont' really have a solid, scientific explanation for subjective experience, not just about how we process, but how we *feel* it. If we can't answer that precisely, how can we say where it stops - animals? insects? rocks? Just because we confidently assert something - 'souls are bollocks' - does not make that truth either. We don't as much as we *like* to think, even though modern science is always correcting and finding new truths. 

Science doesnt know *everything*, but that's not the same thing as saying the thing you believe in, the pattern you have found, is true. We're pretty good at seeing patterns - some brains are harder wired for it than others - and they can be complex, and almost indisputable, to a *point* - but at some point we have to verify them somehow, or they could be dangerous. 

But some things are crazily, inherently true - for examples, animist traditions and indigenous relationships to land. They weren't random. They were ways of living that were totally grounded, sustainable, attentive, and based on the idea that *the natural world was responsive* and *not* inert. So whatever you call it, whether it's spirit or fungal networks or animal consciousness or oneness in all things, it's a belief that leads to a different behaviour and one that we probably should go back to instead of fucking up the entire world so we have no natural world to support life at all. 

I mean, we *can't* build up a whole belief system based on vibes alone - like God will heal my child and fuck modern medicine, or will stop me being run over by a car if I walk into the middle of the road or if I swallow bleach I can rid myself of COVID. Or that Israel is chosen by God and has the right to kill everyone else to spread the kingdom. Some things are morally fucked up and need to be questioned if not outright quashed. 


![b384e77d-7665-4142-bdf7-633989d2a67d-1_all_14601.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/2449xNVdJpXjnh9sEw57SZRtKDQWGvcmrPNZNK246v8nHPeN2j1rjLhXh86f4e7iNRruA.jpg)

To me science is the best tool we have for testing claims we make about reality - I don't believe science in itself is evil or in fact a God, but stops us believing *just* in feelings, just in case those feelings can be dangerous. It's a good way of making sense of the world, which is all any of us are trying to do. We can't get rid of these older instincts that can be messy and unreliable, because they're pretty good at pointing at something undeniably true and real and tangible, but just uses different language in a pre science kinda way. Like I *know* love is the greatest bond we have, and we should default to compassion and kindess, before I know that it's actually a biological imperative and helps with social cohesion. 

Look, I'm a Libran. I'm about balance. I believe in science, but I also don't think it's the final word. When it works to challenge, revise, question, discover - without the vested interest - it's pretty bloody *cool*. I'm happy to put my faith in it *and question it* and I sure as hell love it when it 'proves' something I've known all along.

Yes! It's time for another art cocktail, mixed by the art gallery this time, making my life easier this way. For the past few weeks I've been focusing on trading and creative works, so art has taken a back seat, and I'm not regretting my decision. This has been a long planned phase that I've been waiting for for so long and now that I got to live it, I'm enjoying every moment of it. ![It's Cocktail Day Again.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/48WDnudABgagnSPoSsHnkzWYLpvuAyNQ38DVxpXKrUXv13MiGgxXQbbCVGBuFkJX4t.jpg) However, art is an important part of my life, it means relaxation, motivation in my creative work, so I will always make sure to dedicate some time to it, even if it's just looking back to previous gallery visits, in order to create a post and share my experience with you. So here I am, sharing some photos I took last month, when I visited one of my favorite art gallery, where I'm a regular already. Anyway, let's get started. Let's see what the group of artist prepared for you this time. ![20260428_114950a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23xAVkupUh3CSJtjNaFMGJjLGqc1b69ES4op7yF3e67tLu4UiJbGy3KHKJw9df25PNQVw.JPG) Mana Bucur - Tousled Most likely you have rarely seen me saying such things about art, in my posts, but I don't like this. It's interesting and innovative, if I can use this word, I appreciate the effort as well, but it's not for me, so let's move on. ![20260428_115005a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23vi1YqwcoA3whoYiQc95KhSbFj9meNSv9JdEedGCqdTEFdxmCN7nh8B6FfW7ATBtTNWp.JPG) Csaba Sánta - Fairies Here I remember I had to find a good angle for several reasons. The two metal sculptures are unconventional, I know, but it increases their value in my opinion. Bringing something new, unseen or even unique is key in this area and these two statues definitely check the boxes in this regard. ![20260428_115022a.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23yTmWC6ZbzAC1mbMQia7EzwWPJVsbqHrGkaEQJxMSUyEwMY8hFKruujeMSPMbTsvQNtx.jpg) Zsigmond Bálint - I Became A Child Of God, Persistence Two photos with deep emotional meaning. Two couples, who lived their whole life together. Too bad I could not get a better shot, but I hope you can see why these photos are valuable. ![20260428_115033a.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23wqnsauTSjJF1i8EC6Uvhe6GWHJNedP5L6bwxGFaSBw9gvSA5Xwfz48eL2QVhqfNyXwY.jpg) ![20260428_115041a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23y8siwufb8WWNBTgnXrCoGkTjLzV3GonZJJsebkt5v5r2z9V7LkRtPaPZWhWkX4eZAE1.JPG) ![20260428_115106a.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23y8v2yV55ueW4ntfVBKomofV9AvQq8ezNMthFdb1vPemuESCw8PAuJYFgAKtv92GFuH2.jpg) István Makkai - Ladder To Being The title could be a little strange as there's no way to translate it 100% accurately, there may be some meaning lost in translation as they say, but I hope you can see what it means. I love the idea of using bones as ladder steps. It's maybe a bit forced, but if you think of it, the human body is also built like that, one bone on top of the other. ![20260428_115132a.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23xVKNFyDuFFHufGMwn7MgfGYRdctceymN5eXsyZJaP7wV9Pg8ne3ShEJuAix8r5oJzsQ.jpg) Örs Rezi - Play Abstract This was a bit unexpected, or I wasn't ready for it, but it made me thinking that pretty soon we're going to see more digital art and I'm not referring to digitally created artworks, but created to symbolize the digital world, with digital items, peripheral equipment needed to create art. ![20260428_115147a.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23xVMEGHrfmFJhU5wAtCTcbWePw1hjNJjgqUqifz8qtVunQuvMh6PXm1VRqzczdmAbecu.JPG) Attila Pokornyi - Shelter Looks like a pod to me, but also like a shelter. Could have double meaning as after all, a pod is a shelter for the beans or whatever seeds the pod contains. It's a good one. ![20260428_115208a.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23xAa4bXPBQLyGttj7ePDKFQNX2P1rCw8dF53oehAzZ7h9ekpiVyJPtsc2UV9nJ1qafuj.jpg) ![20260428_115217a.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23xVLymgLm5mMkafrwuzJFRHo8TzhnULjsAGBBCcdU9Tv2CAwgePKoPcqryqQynmNS2qv.jpg) ![20260428_115219a.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/23uQtewo5Qn9GTAckiqG3Z9N7qoTmwQkCUCYfWQBZhLMk11RgHEVy8FUS1p8omyURx2nL.jpg) ![20260428_115222a.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/erikah/Eo6Lv2gCvkid7nAxLL5xTkvZtk9tQDaoBHqhC2JKUm1gpq53jKjteRpbRBixAzUYLaf.jpg) Gabriella Fábián - Springtime And this was the winner for me this time. If you are a science fiction fan, or even if you are not and you just happen to be old enough to have been around to enjoy it when it was reasonably fresh, there is a really good chance that you enjoyed or even love the film *Aliens* from 1986. For me, I was too young to be allowed to watch such a film when it first was released and I had to wait a number of years before I got to see it. But when I did, wow! I mean just wow! To me, this is one of the greatest cinematic experiences of all time and there is very little to call a flaw that was in the entire production. The story is great, the casting is great, the soundtrack is great, just everything about that film is fantastic.
https://is1-ssl.mzstatic.com/image/thumb/nuXX5ZwcxG1aOaaBqD8C0w/1200x675.jpg [src](https://is1-ssl.mzstatic.com/image/thumb/nuXX5ZwcxG1aOaaBqD8C0w/1200x675.jpg)
I've seen a lot of documentaries about various things and in particular about the making of certain films. I normally always enjoy getting to get a peak at what it would be like to be involved in a film, especially when that film is one of the favorites from my childhood. I think one of the only things that might turn off some casuals from watching this, is that the documentary is so exhaustive that it is nearly 3 times as long as the actual film is. It's going to be a bit much for a lot of people, that much is for certain. It was released as a special to go alongside the 40th anniversary of the film's release and if you weren't feeling bad about your age yet, you will now if you were alive when this film was sent out to cinemas.
https://i.ytimg.com/vi/5tF529mmjnM/maxresdefault.jpg [src](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/5tF529mmjnM/maxresdefault.jpg)
A great deal of time is spent talking to James Cameron and Sigourney Weaver, as you would expect, but they also spend a lot of time talking to rather "minor actors" such as the pilot Corporal Ferro that became a bit of a legend in the sci-fi world despite the fact that she only has a handful of lines and a couple of scenes in the entire movie. The same can be said for other actors such as the one that finds a bit of "goo" on the ship lander when he is getting back on it and this was foreshadowing of the fact that an Alien was already on board. This actor, and my apologies for remembering neither the actor nor the character, was so minor in the film that he couldn't even be bothered to turn up for a day of refining his audio and therefore a voice-over actor was used to dub over his spoken lines. This is something that he deeply regrets today of course because nobody could possibly foresee *Aliens* becoming the absolutely massive hit that it became. Which brings us to some really cool other aspects that this documentary points out including the fact that the overall budget for this film, including the salaries of all the actors and the director, was a mere $16 million. Each episode of many big-budget TV shows cost more than this these days.
https://preview.redd.it/behind-the-scenes-aliens-1986-v0-qxxigwy8eizd1.png?width=640&crop=smart&auto=webp&s=7c63a6c2c75f5427bc431d183aa1c8f4235ee9ef [src](https://preview.redd.it/behind-the-scenes-aliens-1986-v0-qxxigwy8eizd1.png?width=640&crop=smart&auto=webp&s=7c63a6c2c75f5427bc431d183aa1c8f4235ee9ef)
Something that I believe will interest most people, and is consequently why this film stands out from so many others including other *Alien* films, is because they didn't use any CGI and everything is practical effects and models painstakingly created over long periods of time using puppetry, models, and people wearing heavy suits to simulate the Xenomorphs. Most fans are probably already aware of this process to some degree, but to see exactly how painstakingly time-consuming all of this was just makes the film an even greater accomplishment than you might already think it is. The actors regale us over and over again about how much time was spent putting on prosthesis or how they had to shoot a particular scene many times over despite the extreme difficulty that was involved in filming it just once.
https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/moviemorgue/images/0/0f/Drake_melting_face.webp/revision/latest/scale-to-width/360?cb=20210819144334 [src](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/moviemorgue/images/0/0f/Drake_melting_face.webp/revision/latest/scale-to-width/360?cb=20210819144334)
In just one scene that it is pointed out to the audience that Alien blood is in fact a very powerful acid that melts human skin (as well as steel) Private Drake gets his face melted off in one of the best death scene's in the film. Actor Mark Rolston tells us a great deal about how he had to be on set at 2am in order to have this all "installed" in time for shooting when the rest of the crew would turn up hours later. He also tells us how while he was there he noticed someone in the corner working by flashlight and it was James Carmeron, who truly burned the candle at both ends during the entire production of this film.
If you decide to watch this, I doubt that you will make it through the entire thing in one sitting because at 4 and a half hours, one could say that it is "a bit long." I suppose they could have made it shorter but the nerd in me is kind of happy that they made a completely exhaustive documentary about the film and honestly, I wish they would do something like this for other legendary films as well. I will admit though, that I am already on my 3rd "pause" as far as watching it is concerned and I still have at least an hour to go. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KOsTpoR76H4

Should I watch it?

Well, this is where I have to be honest: Unless this film holds a *very special* place in your heart the way it does for me then no, you should not watch this, it will not hold your interest. However, if you are one of the millions of people out there that really hold this film in extremely high regard and consider it to be one of the greatest cinematic achievements of all time the way that I do, then the answer should be pretty clear. I somehow managed to not know it existed until a fellow local nerd pointed it out to me. It is VERY long and while I am personally very interested in all of the information that they provide, I can totally understand why a majority of people would not be. I am still going to put a "recommended stamp" on this even though I realize that for most people, this is an easy pass. If you don't love *Aliens* or even better if you haven't seen it, I would recommend that you go back and watch that film instead because it is such a great film for a lot of reasons and one of the things that they broach the topic of is "would this film be better if it was made with today's tech" and the answer that most people come to is that some scenes could have been improved, but for the most part, it is just perfect in exactly the way that they did film it. Future Alien film releases that DID have the power of CGI on their side are terrible in comparison specifically *because* they skipped practical effects and instead opted for more expensive, but faster CGI. James Cameron does say one thing in the film that makes me happy when he said that "if I have anything to say about it, *Aliens* will never be allowed to have a remake" it needs no remake
![photodune-6774981-recommended-grunge-red-stamp-xs-643x272.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/netflixr/2424GudAc7bFr8LHXNQd8JLsDNgGoxs5MdjkNGMffLso1dZZdkwAvVmdd5ooMynWyTa3r.jpg) this documentary can be legally streamed as part of a subscription on AMC+, Shudder, or Apple TV+. As if often the case, it can be rented from all the other big streaming services as well. It is not available on Netflix

`DECOY` – Draws the attacks of enemy units with Snipe, Apex Strike, and Opportunity unless an ally Taunt unit is present. Does not affect enemy units at the first position.



#### SILVER

Finally, when you upgrade this monster to its maximum level of 10, its stats improve further and it now possesses 5 ranged attack power at 4 speed with 6 armor and 7 health. `POISON BURST` – When defeated, 100% chance to apply Poison to attacker and 50% chance to apply Poison to units adjacent to attacker. Poisoned units lose 2 health at the beginning of each round.



Last but not least, I think this monster is a very powerful defensive ranged card for high mana limit battles. And even when this card finally gets defeated, the Poison Burst ability can still punish the enemy team by applying Poison to the attacker and possibly nearby enemy units as well. Overall, I think the Living Berm is a heavily defensive monster with strong ranged firepower and some very annoying abilities that can create chaos for the enemy lineup. What do you think?

And please keep in mind that of course I do not mean everyone from Russia.  I don't play politics but I do play "observe and report."  I can see with my own eyes from having lived here that there is one group, one nationality, that seems to keep to themselves and rarely interacts with any other group.  Call is a language barrier or a culture barrier or whatever you want, but there are a lot of Russians here and I don't know anyone that has more than 1 or 2 Russian people that they even know.   

Social aspects aside, because I actually would enjoy having some more Russian friends, there have been a few events lately that have the public calling for restrictions on foreigners entering and staying in the country, just like I feared it would.

<center> https://cdn2.tuoitre.vn/thumb_w/1200/471584752817336320/2026/4/28/11877-17772974092391062824654-1777357774041137047914-228-0-848-992-crop-177735778898768477451.png
[src](https://cdn2.tuoitre.vn/thumb_w/1200/471584752817336320/2026/4/28/11877-17772974092391062824654-1777357774041137047914-228-0-848-992-crop-177735778898768477451.png)</center> 

This country is surprisingly devoid of genuine road rage despite the fact that the roads here are chaotic as can be.   I rarely drive but when I am so much as walking, it can sometimes be a real exercise in patience to keep your cool on the roads until you just get used to it.  

There was an incident that ended up getting recorded and going viral recently of a Russian guy and his gf having a minor scrape where a taxi touched their bike and they fell, and the response of the Russian was to start shouting and eventually to hit the taxi driver.  It was just a slap and not a beatdown, but the damage that encouraged xenophobia was already done.  

The couple involved were ID'd by the powers of the internet and they were brought in by police but strangely, not charged nor deported.   It was revealed that they are teaching English here which was odd because on the video when the Russian is trying to speak English he is bloody terrible at it.   I hope they aren't paying him much but I am sure the school is really distancing themselves from him at the moment because it is almost certain he was illegally employed in the first place.

<center> 
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gabe.radke/23wC7qtm1Px9G1eJrZjL58BBtntTJ399FTkeh79AvReQiJCm7kZVuFTp8Shiagb7qLFj1.png)
</center> 

He issued some sort of apology or explanation about the situation but it wasn't really an apology, it was more of a deflection of blame and sort of attacking the general public for lashing out at HIM even though he was the one that attacked a taxi driver for a minor fender bender that is so common it isn't even worth getting worked up over.

later it was discovered that there is a 2nd video of him doing the exact same thing to another taxi driver on a separate instance.  

To me the solution to this isolated incident is quite simple:  prosecute this one person.   Unfortunately the police have failed to do that and now the story is kind of blowing up on Vietnamese social media (what little they are allowed to have) and there is a growing anti-foreigner sentiment brewing and this is not a good thing.  

I think 99% of people in the world would never do this sort of thing and would likely at least try to behave like a guest in another country but this person is not like that.  He seems prone to acts of violence and just like I would suggest they do to anyone, someone that is like that has to be punished one way or another.

Vietnam is a very safe society specifically because things like assault are not tolerated so I am a bit confused and concerned about why they would just let this instance slide.   

I am hopeful that things can calm down.  I haven't noticed any anti-foreigner sentiment thus far because everyone I know and hang out with is respectful and not violent.  That doesn't really matter in the court of public opinion though, does it?  If this anti-foreigner sentiment gains ground I fear the that next step would be to start limiting visas especially since it was discovered that this man has been living here and working illegally for years.   

This has been my home for many years and I had hoped (still do hope) that it would remain my home for many years to come.  But in order for that the remain the case the "bad apples" are going to have to be removed from the pot, starting with this guy.

What do you think?
